title: Perp margin rates and max leverage are public again
body:
`srm_perp_margin_requirements` returns, carrying the v2 field set — `im_perp_req`, `mm_perp_req`
and `max_leverage` — as decimal strings. `max_leverage` is `1 / im_perp_req` rounded to 2
decimals.

It is reported in two places, both keyed by risk universe:

* `public/get_currency` and `public/get_all_currencies` — on each entry of `perp.universes[]`.
* `public/get_instrument` and `public/get_all_instruments` — inside `perp_details`, for the
  instrument's own risk universe.

The object is absent (or `null`) where no Standard Risk Manager in that universe prices the
currency, and on option assets. A currency whose perp market has been scaled out reports
`im_perp_req` of `"0"` and `max_leverage` of `"0"` — v2's behaviour, retained.

The v2 path is not restored: the object no longer sits at the top level of the currency
response. See Migrating from V2.

body:

title: TWAP resolution coming to 5-minute and 15-minute crypto markets
body:
Scheduled for **Wednesday, August 19**: short-cadence crypto up/down markets begin resolving on a **Chainlink time-weighted average price (TWAP)** instead of a single instantaneous price. Advance notice for builders: if you trade or quote these markets programmatically, review your assumptions about how the boundary price is determined.

* **What changes:** both the Price to Beat (captured at open) and the closing value come from the same Chainlink TWAP stream — an average over a fixed window — rather than one price tick. The closing TWAP greater than or equal to the Price to Beat resolves **Up**; otherwise **Down**.
* **Why:** an average over the window means a momentary spike at the market boundary does not decide the outcome on its own.
* **Detection:** TWAP markets carry `streamType: "twap"` and `twapWindowSeconds` on `metadata.chainlinkDataStream` in market responses; existing spot-resolved markets carry `streamType: "spot"`. Each market's description names the exact feed, window, and tolerance.
* **Unchanged:** market cadence, slugs, trading, order flow, and settlement. This is a resolution-source change only, applied per market. Read the market's description and `metadata.chainlinkDataStream` to see which rule applies.

**Documentation:** Market resolution — Chainlink TWAP | Get Market

title: Perps price band now limits crossing orders
body:
The Perps price band changes sides. It no longer limits how far an order may rest from its own side of the book. Instead it limits how far an order may cross the other side:

- A bid is rejected above the higher of twice the best ask or the best ask plus 1,000 ticks.
- An ask is rejected below the lower of half the best bid or the best bid minus 1,000 ticks.

When the other side of the book is empty, there is no limit. Rejected orders and amends return `invalid price`, as before. Orders that sweep the book with a far limit price, for example a bid at `1000.00` into a best ask of `10.00`, now fail and should carry a limit within the band. See Price Banding.
note: orders that used to rest now fail ("now fail")

title: [Important] API Path Format and Error Handling Checks
body:
Dear developers,

This is the Upbit Developer Center team.

The API Path format requirements specified in the Upbit API documentation are now in effect. Please ensure that your API requests follow the required Path format.

If you currently use `error.message` to identify or handle API errors, please update your implementation to use `error.name` instead.

To avoid disruptions to your API integration, please review your request Paths and error-handling logic and make any necessary changes.

## 1.Schedule

- Effective Date: October 28, 2026 (Wednesday)
- Applicable Regions: Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand

## 2.Key Details

1) API Request Path Format

API request Paths must follow the requirements below.

- Path Start and Separators: Exactly one `/` at the beginning and between Path segments.
- Path End: A trailing `/` is not allowed.

Valid Path

`/v1/orders`

Invalid Paths

```
//v1/orders
/v1//orders
/v1/orders//
```

Requests containing unnecessary slashes (`/`), as shown above, will result in an error.

2) API Error Handling

Since `error.message` may change, if you currently use it to identify or handle API errors, please use `error.name` instead.

```
{
  "error": {
    "name": "ERROR_CODE",
    "message": "ERROR_MESSAGE" → Not recommended for error handling
  }
}
```

## 3.API Integration Checklist

Please review the following items in your current API integration.

- Ensure there are no duplicate slashes (`//`) at the beginning or within the Path, and no trailing slash (`/`).
- Ensure no duplicate slashes are introduced when combining `BASE_URL` and `PATH`.
- Ensure API errors are handled based on `error.name`.

For example, the following configuration may result in a duplicate slash in the request URL.

| Item | Incorrect (Duplicate Slash) | Correct |
| BASE_URL | https://sg-api.upbit.com/ | https://sg-api.upbit.com |
| PATH | /v1/orders | /v1/orders |
| Request URL | https://sg-api.upbit.com//v1/orders | https://sg-api.upbit.com/v1/orders |

The same Path format requirements apply to the Singapore (`sg`), Indonesia(`id`), and Thailand(`th`) API endpoints.

## 4.Important Notes

- The required API Path format is in effect across all applicable regions.
- If you operate an API-integrated service or automated system, please review and test your request Paths and error-handling logic to prevent service disruptions.

Please ensure that your API integration follows the updated requirements and make any necessary changes.

If you have any inquiries, please contact us at open-api.global@upbit.com.

We will respond as soon as possible.

Thank you.

Upbit Developer Center
note: sample miss: path rules now enforced, bad paths "will result in an error"

title: Bug fix: pack quotes ignore liquidity far above the best price
body:
Pack leg pricing swept the entire order book, so orders resting far above the best price could distort a quoted leg price. A leg with only a few dollars of real asks could quote at a badly wrong price.

* `POST /parlay/quote` and pack leg pricing now only count liquidity within 10 cents of the best usable price.
* Books that are genuinely thin near the best price now reject with an explicit thin-book reason in `ineligibleReasons` instead of quoting a distorted price.
* Liquidity resting more than 10 cents above the best price no longer counts toward depth, so a small number of previously quotable legs now reject.
* No action required.

**Documentation:** Packs
note: bug fix, "No action required" (sample false positive)

title: Crypto deposit and withdrawal — one Travel Rule guide and documented errors
body:
⚠ Effective November 1, 2026
The Travel Rule changes described here take effect on 2026-11-01. Until then, crypto withdrawals keep following the current Travel Rule flow; the deposit declaration already takes the new declaration body and the previous originator payload is no longer accepted.

- One guide for both operations: How to declare the Travel Rule replaces the deposit and withdrawal guides. Its seven steps are the same for a deposit and a withdrawal, linking both calls where they differ, and it holds the variants, a table of the fields each path asks, the errors and the outcomes
- The fields table covers the seven paths of a declaration and tells, for each field, whether it is required, optional, for company accounts only, required above USD 50,000, ignored or not part of the variant
- `POST /rest/v3/deposits/{deposit_sn}/travel_rule` and `POST /rest/v3/withdrawals/{withdrawal_sn}/travel_rule` document the `400` and `422` body, `{ "error": { "message", "code", "details" } }`, with one example per case. `details` lists every problem at once; `code` is `400` for a body that does not fit the path, `422` for an operation that cannot take the declaration and `4001` when the declaration itself is refused (a field the account type does not take, an invalid CPF/CNPJ, a purpose the operation does not accept, or `purpose_description` missing above USD 50,000)
- The descriptions of the declaration routes are shorter: they keep what has to be true before the call, the variants and the outcome, and point to the step of the guide that details each part
- Deposit declaration · Withdrawal declaration

title: October 5, 2026: TP/SL legs can be modified over WebSocket
body:
## TP/SL legs can be modified over WebSocket

`order_modify` accepts TP/SL legs; `collateral_order_tpsl_place` documented as additive

Legs created by `collateral_order_tpsl_place` can be changed with `order_modify` — send the leg's `order_id` or `client_order_id` with a new `activation_price`. Earlier documentation said `order_modify` returned error `160` for a TPSL leg; that statement was incorrect and is removed.

Each `collateral_order_tpsl_place` call creates a new pair of TP/SL orders. It does not replace or cancel TP/SL orders already on the position, including those created through the REST API (`takeProfit` / `stopLoss`) or by OTO orders. To change levels, modify the existing orders with `order_modify`, or cancel those orders with `order_cancel` and place new ones. When a TP/SL order triggers and closes the position, the remaining TP/SL orders for that position are cancelled automatically.
note: "that statement was incorrect and is removed" is a docs correction (sample false positive)

title: 9/1/2026: For SIGNED endpoints you must now percent-encode the request payload before computing the signature, then append &signature=.... Requests…
body:
The following changes are now live as part of the 8/31/2026 spot exchange upgrade.

REST API

- For SIGNED endpoints you must now percent-encode the request payload before computing the signature, then append `&signature=...`. Requests that compute the signature before encoding are rejected with `-1022 INVALID_SIGNATURE`.
- Please avoid SQL keywords (e.g. `SELECT`, `DROP`) in request parameter values, as they may trigger a Web Application Firewall (WAF) security block.
- All `/api/v1/*` endpoints (`ping`, `time`, `klines`, `depth`, `aggTrades`, `historicalTrades`, `trades`, `ticker/*`, `userDataStream`) have been retired. Use the `/api/v3/*` equivalents.
- A new optional parameter `symbolStatus` (supported values `TRADING`, `HALT`, `BREAK`) has been added to `GET /api/v3/depth`, `/api/v3/ticker/price`, `/api/v3/ticker/bookTicker`, and `/api/v3/ticker/24hr`. If a single symbol is specified and its status does not match, error `-1220 SYMBOL_DOES_NOT_MATCH_STATUS` is returned. If multiple symbols are specified, non-matching symbols are excluded from the response. Omitting the parameter returns all symbols.
- Get Order and Cancel Order: when both `orderId` and `origClientOrderId` are sent, the order is looked up by `orderId` and `origClientOrderId` is validated against it — both must match, or the request returns `-2039`. When neither is sent, the request now returns `-1102` (Cancel Order previously returned `-1128`).
- The weight of `GET /api/v3/exchangeInfo` has increased from 10 to 20 (REST and WebSocket API).
- `GET /api/v3/account` response now includes a `uid` field (your User ID / account).
- `GET /api/v3/klines` has a new optional parameter `timeZone` (default 0, UTC).
- `GET /api/v3/avgPrice` response now includes a `closeTime` field.
- Timestamp parameters are now rejected if they are before 2017-01-01 (`< 1483228800000`) or more than 10 seconds in the future. Out-of-range `startTime`/`endTime` values are clamped to the valid range.
- `GET /api/v3/historicalTrades` no longer requires an API key — its security type has changed from `MARKET_DATA` to `NONE`. The `X-MBX-APIKEY` header is no longer necessary.
- New endpoint `GET /api/v3/account/commission` returns current account commission rates (standard and tax commission, plus discount information). Weight: 20; `symbol` required.
- New endpoint `GET /api/v3/ticker/tradingDay` returns price change statistics for a trading day. Weight: 4 per symbol, capped at 200 once more than 50 symbols are requested. Parameters: `symbol` or `symbols` (one required, max 100 symbols), `timeZone`, `type` (`FULL` or `MINI`), and `symbolStatus`.

WebSocket API

- The `symbolStatus` parameter (supported values `TRADING`, `HALT`, `BREAK`) has been added to the WebSocket API methods `depth`, `ticker.24hr`, `ticker.price`, `ticker.book`, and `ticker`, with the same matching behavior as the REST endpoints above.
- The `myFilters` request has been added to the WebSocket API.

WebSocket Streams

- The Buyer order ID (`b`) and Seller order ID (`a`) fields have been removed from the `@trade` stream payload. To track whether your order was part of a trade, listen to the User Data Streams.
- The steps for managing a local order book correctly have been updated (Order Book Streams → Managing a Local Order Book). Depth snapshots now reference a limit of 5000 price levels per side, and the buffering and synchronization steps have been clarified.

Errors

- New error codes: `-2039` (both `orderId` and `origClientOrderId` given but no matching order), `-1220 SYMBOL_DOES_NOT_MATCH_STATUS`, and `-1151` (symbol is present multiple times in the list).

title: Release 11.08.2026: Estimated Liquidation Price (ELP) deprecation
body:
Estimated Liquidation Price (ELP) deprecation

`estimated_liquidation_price` is being deprecated and will no longer be returned for Segregated Standard Margin (`segregated_sm`) accounts (it is currently only added for futures). ELP remains available via Position Builder and the Position Builder API. Affected methods: private/get_position and private/get_positions.

Unaggregated (`.raw`) market data

All unaggregated market data subscriptions, identified by the `.raw` postfix, are now aggregated on a 1 millisecond basis due to the integration between the multicast, WebSocket and FIX market data APIs and Starbase. 1 millisecond is below the median latency of any non-Starbase market data feed, so no major degradation in performance is expected.

Starbase identifiers on orders and trades

- Order objects: new `starbase_client_order_id` field (client order id for orders submitted directly to Starbase via direct access; not returned for orders placed through the Deribit API). Combo legs inherit the parent combo order's client order id.
- User trade objects: new `starbase_order_id` and `starbase_client_order_id` fields, present only for trades matched in Starbase. `starbase_client_order_id` reflects your own order (maker or taker side); for self-trades it is the taker order's client order id.
- Combo trade legs carry the full set of Starbase fields (`starbase_match_id`, `starbase_order_id`, `starbase_client_order_id`, `starbase_timestamp`) when matched in Starbase, and `starbase_last_update_timestamp` is available on combo leg order updates.
- private/get_transaction_log: trade entries executed in Starbase include `starbase_match_id`, `starbase_order_id` and `starbase_timestamp`.

New instrument fields

public/get_instrument and public/get_instruments now include `product_group` (product group classification of the instrument's base currency: BTC, ETH, TIER_2, TIER_3) and `index_id` (numeric identifier of the price index used by the instrument, shared by instruments with the same `price_index`).

title: 2026-10-22: GET /fapi/v3/incomePage — Get Income History With Pagination
body:
### Added

#### `GET /fapi/v3/incomePage` — Get Income History With Pagination

New USER_DATA endpoint (weight 30) returning income history page by page, with `symbol`/`incomeType`/`startTime`/`endTime`/`page`/`limit` filters (`page` starts at 1; `limit` defaults to `100`, max `1000`; `page` × `limit` ≤ 100,000). The response is a paginated object (`total`, `page`, `limit`, `hasMore`, `rows`); each `rows[]` record has the same fields as a `GET /fapi/v3/income` record. `incomeType` accepts the same values as `GET /fapi/v3/income`. Records are sorted by `time` ascending; there is no limit on the time span, and if neither `startTime` nor `endTime` is sent the recent 7-day data is returned. Requires the V3 authentication parameters `nonce`, `signer`, and `signature`.

Documented in EN and CN, mainnet and testnet futures API references.

title: 2026-10-08: Documentation enhancements (no API behavior changes)
body:
- Documentation enhancements (no API behavior changes):
  - `POST /sapi/v1/w3w/wallet/prediction/trade/get-quote`: removed the approximate 1.5 USDT `MARKET` minimum and the statement that `LIMIT` orders have no minimum. The minimum order amount is set by the server and may change, so no fixed value is documented. It is checked on `BUY` orders by amount and on `SELL` orders by share quantity, for both order types. A successful quote does not guarantee that an order is accepted or filled. Also documented that a `priceLimit` that is not on the price tick is truncated down instead of being rejected.
  - `GET /sapi/v1/w3w/wallet/prediction/market/detail` and `GET /sapi/v1/w3w/wallet/prediction/market/list`: documented the values of `status` and `markets[].tradingStatus`, that `markets[].tradingStatus` and not `status` decides whether new orders may be attempted, the meaning of `decimalPrecision`, and the `outcomes[].winner` field that is set after resolution.
  - `GET /sapi/v1/w3w/wallet/prediction/position/settled-history`: documented that there is no separate cancelled, invalid or refunded status and how a split payout of a resolved market is represented.

title: Sep 4, 2026: New API: Data API v2 is live at https://data-api.polymarket.com/v2 for wallet activity, market data, and trader and builder analytics.…
body:
- New API: Data API v2 is live at `https://data-api.polymarket.com/v2` for wallet activity, market data, and trader and builder analytics. Start with the Data API overview or Migrating from v1.
- Response contract: Every endpoint wraps its payload in `data`. Paginated reads add `pagination` with opaque cursors (no offset parameter). Each endpoint takes snake_case parameters with camelCase aliases, names on-chain ids `condition`/`condition_id`, encodes money and size as JSON numbers (bare fields are shares, `_usdc` fields are USD), and signals load with `429` plus `Retry-After`.
- New capabilities over v1: cumulative wallet PnL series (`/v2/user-pnl`), profile stats (`/v2/user-stats`), windowed wallet volume (`/v2/user-volume`), the biggest-winners board, builder leaderboard and volume, per-holder position economics (`/v2/holders?include_pnl=true`), and resolution lifecycle reads (`/v2/resolutions`).
- Price history moves to the data host: `GET /v2/prices-history` replaces the CLOB-hosted route, with three explicit window forms (`interval`, `start`/`end`, `as_of`), second-based `bucket_seconds`, and cursor pagination.
- TypeScript SDK: The SDK's Data API methods now use v2. See the SDK changelog.
- Rate limits: per-family limits are published on Rate Limits.
- v1 status: `/v1` keeps serving unchanged but is frozen. New fields and endpoints land on v2 only. The v1 reference lives under Data API v1 (Legacy).
- Higher taker delay: The taker delay on crypto markets is now `150ms`, up from `50ms`. The change took effect on September 4 at 14:00 UTC (10:00 AM ET).

title: Filter portfolio history by market
body:
`GET /portfolio/history` now accepts an optional `market=` query parameter. When set, the response only includes activity for that market across every source: CLOB and AMM trades, splits/merges, NegRisk conversions, claims, and resolutions. Use it to verify a single market's activity without walking your full account history.

* An unknown `market` slug returns `404`.
* Cursors are market-scoped: a `nextCursor` issued for one `market` value is only valid when replayed with the same `market` value on the next page. Mixing a filtered cursor with a different or missing `market` produces incorrect pagination.
* Requests without `market` behave exactly as before.

**Documentation:** Get History

title: [October 15, 2026] Added Server Time/Announcements/Coins v3 APIs; multiple REST enhancements
body:
**New APIs:**

- `/api/v3/market/time` Get the current server time (migrated from `/api/v2/public/time`; the response now includes both a millisecond field `serverTime` and a new microsecond field `serverTimeMicros`)
- `/api/v3/public/annoucements` Get announcements (migrated from `/api/v2/public/annoucements`)
- `/api/v3/market/coins` Get coin information (migrated from `/api/v2/spot/public/coins`)

Interface:
- /api/v3/market/instruments
- /api/v3/trade/place-order
- /api/v3/trade/place-batch
- /api/v3/user/set-rate-limit-quota
- /api/v3/user/rate-limit-quota
- /api/v3/account/max-open-available
- /api/v3/trade/unfilled-strategy-orders

Changes:
- `Get Instruments`: added response fields `fullName`, `instrumentType` (`metal`/`energy`/`stock`/`etf`/`crypto`), `marketRegion`, and `isin` for traditional-finance-related trading pairs (stocks, ETFs, Reality/rtoken, etc.). The existing `symbolType` field is unchanged and continues to be returned alongside `instrumentType`.
- `Place Order` / `Batch Order`: added request parameters `requestTime` and `receiveWindow` to both the single and batch order placement endpoints, allowing a validity window to be set for order placement. If an order is received by the matching engine after `requestTime + receiveWindow`, it is canceled instead of being placed into the order book.
- `Set RateLimit Quota` / `Get RateLimit Quota`: these endpoints now also support being called directly by a sub-account using its own API Key, to set or query its own rate limit quota. The `uids`/`uid` field is not required (and is ignored) when called by a sub-account; it remains required when called by the master account. Rules are otherwise unchanged.
- `Get Max Open Available`: added request parameter `marginMode` (`crossed`/`isolated`, defaults to `crossed`). Under isolated margin mode, the `available` calculation excludes futures trial funds.
- `Unfilled Strategy Orders`: added response field `side`, aligning with the field already present in the WebSocket order push data.
